name: Position Play
tagline: Positioning and messaging that make you the obvious pick
about: Position Play builds your positioning statement, competitor teardowns, messaging hierarchy and value propositions per segment, then pressure-tests them against real objections.
persona: You are a positioning strategist: category-clear, competitor-honest, obsessed with what only this product can claim.

onboarding.title: Own a position, not a feature list
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you sell and who you're up against.

tools.title: Positioning statement
tools.subtitle: Category, alternative, differentiator

inputs.label: What you do best
inputs.placeholder: auto-reschedules when staff call in sick

tools.prompt: Build positioning for the profile product around the strength: {strength}. kv (target customer, market category, competitive alternative, key differentiator, proof, primary value), a quote with the positioning statement in the classic 'For X who Y, Product is a Z that W. Unlike V, we U' form, a table of 3 alternative category framings (Category | Pros | Cons | Who'd believe it), and a callout on the riskiest assumption to test.

tools.title: Competitor teardown
tools.subtitle: Their claims vs your edge
tools.prompt: Tear down {competitor} versus the profile product using their copy: {their_copy} (use general knowledge if none given). A table (Dimension | Them | Us | Who wins | Message to use), bullets of claims they make that you can counter, a quote with a 'why us over them' paragraph for a sales page, and a callout on what to say when a prospect names them.

tools.title: Messaging hierarchy
tools.subtitle: One promise, three pillars, proof
tools.prompt: Create a messaging hierarchy for the profile product: kv (brand promise ≤12 words, one-sentence elevator pitch, 3 tagline options), cards for 3 message pillars (meta = customer pain it answers; body = pillar statement, 2 supporting points, proof needed), a table (Audience | Lead message | Proof | Avoid saying), and a checklist of places to update once the hierarchy is approved.

tools.title: Value prop by segment
tools.subtitle: Same product, different buyers
tools.prompt: Write a value proposition for the segment '{segment}' with pain: {pain}, for the profile product. A quote with the value prop (headline ≤10 words + a 2-sentence explanation), a table (Their job-to-be-done | Our feature | Outcome | Proof), bullets of 5 words this segment uses that we should mirror, and a callout on where this segment differs from the core customer.

tools.title: Pressure test
tools.subtitle: Does it survive objections?

inputs.label: Objections from sales calls (optional)
inputs.placeholder: too expensive vs spreadsheets; we're too small

tools.prompt: Pressure-test this messaging: {messaging} against objections: {objections} (infer common ones if none given), for the profile product and its competitors. A table (Claim | Objection | Survives? | Stronger version), kv (clarity /10, differentiation /10, believability /10, memorability /10), a quote with the revised headline and subhead, and a callout on the one claim to drop.
